long_biography.plain_text:
Vardinogiannis grew up in Episkopi, Crete, and trained for a maritime career before serving as a ship's captain during the family's early expansion. That practical background connected him directly to tanker operations and marine-fuel supply rather than to the refinery leadership associated with his brother Vardis. His later work centred on SEKAVIN, whose bunkering, trading and shipping-agency businesses serve vessels in Greek ports and international markets.

He also became a major figure in Greek football. In 1979, he led the family group's purchase of a majority stake in Panathinaikos and became president. During his 21-year tenure, the club won six league titles and nine Greek Cups while establishing a sustained European presence. After his presidency, he transferred control to the next generation. Decades later, he signed SEKAVIN's 2024 accounts as chairman and managing director.
